to: Price Promise brand retained, content redefined to what practice supports: no silent changes — customer hears first and decides (keep, adjust, or full deposit refund). FAQ item 6 (already honest) untouched and used as the model. Full sweep via scripts/sweep-price-promise.mjs.
executed_by: eddie (agreed with Kacy in 2026-08-24 working session; her ask after refunding a customer who had AGREED to an increase but was owed under the absolute language)
evidence_source: Kacy 8/24: refunds being issued because customers cite the absolute language even after consenting to increases; review order 37348381; 38/38 lowball read; call log showing 11 of 18 recent calls from price-promise pages
hypothesis: Removing the absolute claim eliminates the refund-on-consent legal exposure without killing the promise's conversion value, because the honest version (no silent changes + refundable deposit) retains the differentiator. Risk: website conversion rate may dip if the absolute promise was doing conversion work — watch form-start and completion rates for 2 weeks against the pre-change baseline.
